Dispatch No. 28 / Tbilisi

A city that
keeps its doors
half open.

Sulphur steam, walnut trees, and balconies leaning over the old town. A week spent walking where Europe loosens into Asia.

From the notebookDay one / 06:40

First light in Sololaki

The city wakes
one courtyard
at a time.

The overnight train leaves you blinking on the platform with the bread sellers and taxi drivers. Walk west. The streets are quiet enough to hear cups meeting saucers behind kitchen windows.

In Sololaki, every doorway offers a small decision: tiled stairwell, grapevine courtyard, a glimpse of painted ceiling. Nothing announces itself. That is the pleasure of it.

By nine, the bakeries breathe warm air onto the pavement. Order lobiani, point to whatever looks freshest, and keep climbing toward the ridge.

“The best way through Tbilisi is to leave half the day unplanned.”— Nino, bookseller on Lado Asatiani St.
